questions.question: Your child finds a lost wallet with money on the ground. What is the right thing to do?
questions.context: Trustworthiness and returning lost items are core Islamic values.

options.text: Look for its owner or hand it over to a trusted adult or person in charge
options.rationale: ✅ Returning lost belongings is an act of honesty and trustworthiness.

options.text: Kick it aside and leave it in the street
options.rationale: ❌ Handing it to a responsible person helps ensure it reaches its owner safely.

options.text: Spend the money right away since the owner does not know who found it
options.rationale: ❌ Taking someone else's property is wrong.

options.text: Keep the money because nobody saw them pick it up
options.rationale: ❌ True honesty means doing what is right even when no person is watching, because Allah sees us.

questions.question: Your child scored high on a test while their friend scored lower. How do you nurture humility?
questions.context: Gratitude and humility beautify success, while arrogance hurts hearts.

options.text: Compare them to their friend so they feel superior
options.rationale: ❌ Comparison breeds arrogance or envy.

options.text: Let them brag about their grade in front of their friend
options.rationale: ❌ Boasting hurts others and goes against good character.

options.text: Tell them 'You are better than everyone else in class'
options.rationale: ❌ Encourages pride and looking down on peers.

options.text: Celebrate their effort with gratitude and encourage them to support and study with their friend
options.rationale: ✅ Humility, gratitude, and helping others reflect noble character.

questions.question: Your daughter hears that a friend spoke unkindly about her behind her back. How do you guide her?
questions.context: Backbiting and gossip harm friendships and go against Islamic ethics.

options.text: Tell her to gossip about the friend in return
options.rationale: ❌ Answering a wrong with the same wrong only spreads harm.

options.text: Teach her that backbiting is wrong and guide her to speak calmly and directly with her friend
options.rationale: ✅ Honest, respectful communication is far better than answering gossip with more gossip.

options.text: Ignore her hurt feelings completely
options.rationale: ❌ Children need both emotional support and ethical guidance.

options.text: Spread rumors about the friend to the whole class
options.rationale: ❌ Spreading gossip deepens conflict and is wrong.

questions.question: Your child sees an elderly neighbor struggling to carry groceries. What do we teach them?
questions.context: Kindness to others and respecting elders are cherished values.

options.text: Walk past and ignore them because it is not our problem
options.rationale: ❌ Caring for neighbors and elders is part of good character.

options.text: Demand money before helping
options.rationale: ❌ Kindness is given sincerely, not sold.

options.text: Offer help in a safe way or ask a nearby parent to help together
options.rationale: ✅ Combines kindness and helpfulness with age-appropriate safety.

options.text: Laugh at them
options.rationale: ❌ Mocking anyone goes against basic decency and faith.

questions.question: Your child got angry and broke a friend's toy. What should you do together?
questions.context: Taking responsibility for damage and learning self-control build integrity.

options.text: Tell your child 'Your friend deserved it'
options.rationale: ❌ Excusing wrong behavior prevents moral growth.

options.text: Refuse to apologize out of pride
options.rationale: ❌ Apologizing when wrong is a sign of strength, not weakness.

options.text: Hit the child in anger
options.rationale: ❌ Violence does not teach self-control.

options.text: Apologize sincerely, repair or replace the toy, and practice calming down when angry
options.rationale: ✅ Accountability, sincere apology, and repair are marks of strong character.

questions.question: During Ramadan, peers tease your fasting child and dare them to break their fast to look 'cool'. How do you guide them?
questions.context: True strength lies in staying true to one's values and worship.

options.text: Shout at the child harshly
options.rationale: ❌ Warm encouragement builds love for worship, while harshness pushes children away.

options.text: Explain that fasting is a special act of worship for Allah and true strength is staying true to your values
options.rationale: ✅ Connects worship to inner confidence and sincere purpose.

options.text: Tell them to break their fast just to please the kids teasing them
options.rationale: ❌ Giving up values for peer approval weakens confidence.

options.text: Brush off their question without guidance
options.rationale: ❌ Children need supportive guidance when facing peer pressure.

questions.question: Your child sees someone shoplifting in a store. What is the right lesson?
questions.context: Respecting others' property and reporting wrongdoing safely are important values.

options.text: Quietly and safely tell a parent or store staff member
options.rationale: ✅ Addresses wrongdoing safely and responsibly.

options.text: Join in and take something too
options.rationale: ❌ Participating in theft is wrong.

options.text: Say that stealing is fine as long as the store is big
options.rationale: ❌ Taking others' property is always wrong.

options.text: Film the person and post it on social media
options.rationale: ❌ Publicly posting videos can be unsafe for a child; telling a trusted adult is right.

questions.question: How do you nurture a deep habit of truthfulness in your child?
questions.context: Truthfulness grows through adult role modeling and a safe home environment.

options.text: Use harsh physical punishment whenever they make a mistake
options.rationale: ❌ Fear of harsh punishment often drives children to lie to protect themselves.

options.text: Make false promises to trick the child into behaving
options.rationale: ❌ Breaking promises teaches children that dishonesty is acceptable.

options.text: Model honesty ourselves and appreciate our child's courage when they admit a mistake
options.rationale: ✅ Role modeling and safe encouragement make honesty the natural choice.

options.text: Tell them lying is fine whenever it is convenient
options.rationale: ❌ Undermines the value of truthfulness.

questions.question: Your child has many toys and a visiting friend has very few. How can you nurture generosity?
questions.context: Sharing and generosity bring warmth and closeness between hearts.

options.text: Say 'Tell your friend to go buy their own toys'
options.rationale: ❌ Teaches selfishness and insensitivity.

options.text: Say 'Helping others is none of our business'
options.rationale: ❌ Generosity starts in our everyday relationships.

options.text: Refuse to let them play together because the friend has less
options.rationale: ❌ Kindness and inclusion are core moral values.

options.text: Encourage sharing warmly while playing and let them choose a nice toy they would love to gift
options.rationale: ✅ Voluntary, warm generosity builds empathy and joy in giving.

questions.question: Your child repeats a bad word they heard on TV. How should you respond?
questions.context: Children often repeat words without fully realizing their weight.

options.text: Explain calmly that we choose kind, respectful words, and suggest a better phrase to use
options.rationale: ✅ Calm guidance teaches respectful speech far better than overreacting.

options.text: Hit the child immediately
options.rationale: ❌ Harshness does not model the gentleness we want to teach.

options.text: Laugh and clap because it sounded funny
options.rationale: ❌ Laughing encourages them to repeat the word for attention.

options.text: Say nothing because it came from TV
options.rationale: ❌ Children need gentle guidance on what words are respectful.

questions.question: Your child wants to donate a small coin from their allowance to someone in need. How do you respond?
questions.context: Even the smallest sincere charity nurtures a generous heart.

options.text: Stop them because the amount is too small to matter
options.rationale: ❌ Sincere small deeds carry great value.

options.text: Mock their small coin
options.rationale: ❌ Belittling good deeds extinguishes a child's enthusiasm for giving.

options.text: Take their money away
options.rationale: ❌ Discourages their initiative to do good.

options.text: Encourage them warmly and affirm that even a small sincere gift matters greatly
options.rationale: ✅ Nurtures generosity and sincerity from a young age.

questions.question: Your child asks: 'Why do we pray?' What is a meaningful, age-appropriate answer?
questions.context: Children connect with prayer when they understand it as a loving link with Allah.

options.text: Because prayer is our direct connection with Allah — thanking Him, finding peace, and bringing rhythm to our day
options.rationale: ✅ Connects prayer to love, gratitude, and daily peace.

options.text: Rely only on scaring the child without mentioning Allah's love and mercy
options.rationale: ❌ Balanced spiritual upbringing begins with love, gratitude, and hope.

options.text: 'So people will praise you and say you are good'
options.rationale: ❌ Worship is for Allah, not for showing off to people.

options.text: 'Just because I said so, do not ask questions'
options.rationale: ❌ Thoughtful answers build genuine understanding and love for worship.

questions.question: Your child gets absorbed in play and delays prayer time. How do you help them build the habit?
questions.context: Warm reminders and praying together make prayer a beloved family anchor.

options.text: Never remind or invite them to pray at all
options.rationale: ❌ Steady, loving encouragement helps habits take root early.

options.text: Humiliate them in front of guests
options.rationale: ❌ Public shaming alienates children.

options.text: Give a gentle heads-up before prayer time and invite them to pray together warmly
options.rationale: ✅ Gentle transition warnings and praying together build a loving habit.

options.text: Hit them to force them to pray
options.rationale: ❌ Harshness creates negative associations with worship.

questions.question: How do you teach your child respect for elders?
questions.context: Children learn respect primarily by watching how their parents treat elders.

options.text: Let them insult elders without any guidance
options.rationale: ❌ Children need clear, loving guidance on respectful manners.

options.text: Model respect toward our own elders and practice warm greetings and polite speaking together
options.rationale: ✅ Living the example at home is the most powerful lesson.

options.text: Lecture them about respect while speaking rudely to elders ourselves
options.rationale: ❌ Actions speak louder than lectures.

options.text: Hit them whenever their voice gets excited
options.rationale: ❌ Gentleness teaches manners better than harshness.

questions.question: Your child sees classmates picking on a quieter student. What should they do?
questions.context: Supporting someone being mistreated — safely and kindly — is a noble value.

options.text: Start a fistfight in the hallway
options.rationale: ❌ Physical fighting escalates danger; getting adult help and using kind words is safer.

options.text: Laugh along with the bullies so they do not target you
options.rationale: ❌ Joining in adds to the harm.

options.text: Speak up kindly for the classmate or get a teacher/trusted adult right away, and befriend the child
options.rationale: ✅ Standing up for fairness safely and showing kindness helps end bullying.

options.text: Pretend not to see anything and never tell an adult
options.rationale: ❌ Getting help from a teacher can protect the child being bullied.

questions.question: How do you nurture gratitude for blessings in your child's daily life?
questions.context: Gratitude shifts focus toward appreciation and contentment.

options.text: Buy excessive luxuries nonstop without ever pausing to appreciate them
options.rationale: ❌ Mindful appreciation builds gratitude.

options.text: Tell them they should feel guilty for having anything
options.rationale: ❌ Gratitude is joyful appreciation, not guilt.

options.text: Forbid them from ever expressing a wish
options.rationale: ❌ Having wishes is normal; gratitude helps balance them.

options.text: Model saying 'Alhamdulillah' (Praise be to Allah) and share three things we are grateful for each day
options.rationale: ✅ Daily gratitude habits build a thankful, content heart.

questions.question: Your young child is eager to try fasting for the first time. What is the wisest approach?
questions.context: Gradual, encouraging steps help young children love worship safely.

options.text: Shame them if they get hungry and need to eat
options.rationale: ❌ Young children learning to fast deserve praise for whatever hours they try.

options.text: Dismiss their excitement completely
options.rationale: ❌ Welcoming their enthusiasm with age-appropriate steps nurtures love for worship.

options.text: Encourage their enthusiasm by starting with a few hours or half a day suited to their age and health
options.rationale: ✅ Gradual practice builds capability and fond memories.

options.text: Force a very young child to fast a full day even if they feel unwell
options.rationale: ❌ Overstraining a young child is unsafe and discouraging.

questions.question: Your child sees someone drop a valuable item from their pocket without noticing. What is the right action?
questions.context: Returning dropped items right away is a direct practice of honesty.

options.text: Step over it and say nothing
options.rationale: ❌ Speaking up right away saves the owner from losing their item.

options.text: Sell it and buy treats
options.rationale: ❌ Taking someone else's property is dishonest.

options.text: Pocket it because 'finders keepers'
options.rationale: ❌ Something dropped still belongs to its owner.

options.text: Call out politely or hand it back to the person (or to security if they walked away)
options.rationale: ✅ Honesty and promptness return the item to its rightful owner.

questions.question: How do you teach your child the value of forgiveness after a friend apologizes?
questions.context: Forgiveness frees the heart from bitterness and repairs friendships.

options.text: Explain that forgiving someone who apologizes shows inner strength and brings peace to the heart
options.rationale: ✅ Forgiveness is a noble strength that heals relationships.

options.text: Tell them to hold a grudge for the rest of the school year
options.rationale: ❌ Learning to accept sincere apologies helps friendships grow.

options.text: Encourage taking physical revenge
options.rationale: ❌ Revenge creates a cycle of harm.

options.text: Tell them 'Never forgive anyone ever'
options.rationale: ❌ Holding endless grudges weighs down the child's heart.

questions.question: Your child says, 'Why should I help someone who is not in my family?' How do you respond?
questions.context: Kindness and compassion extend to all people and creatures.

options.text: Agree that we should never care about anyone outside our house
options.rationale: ❌ Narrows empathy and promotes selfishness.

options.text: Explain that kindness is for everyone, and Allah loves those who do good to others
options.rationale: ✅ Broadens empathy and compassion beyond one's immediate circle.

options.text: Say we only help people if they pay us
options.rationale: ❌ Sincere kindness is not mercenary.

options.text: Shrug and ignore the question
options.rationale: ❌ Thoughtful questions are great moments to share values.

questions.question: How do you teach your child the comforting habit of seeking forgiveness (Istighfar) when they slip up?
questions.context: Turning back to Allah with hope and making amends keeps the heart hopeful and accountable.

options.text: Teach them that mistakes never need apologies
options.rationale: ❌ Acknowledging mistakes is how we grow.

options.text: Make them feel that Allah never forgives mistakes
options.rationale: ❌ Despair is the opposite of healthy spiritual guidance.

options.text: Tell them 'You are a bad person forever' when they make a mistake
options.rationale: ❌ Shaming destroys hope and self-worth.

options.text: Teach them to say 'Astaghfirullah' (I seek Allah's forgiveness), make amends, and remember that Allah is Oft-Forgiving
options.rationale: ✅ Combines humility, accountability, and hope in Allah's mercy.

questions.question: Your child wants to spend their entire allowance the minute they get it. How do you guide them?
questions.context: Moderation and planning teach wise stewardship of blessings.

options.text: Help them divide their allowance into three parts: spending, saving, and giving
options.rationale: ✅ A simple spend-save-give habit builds lifelong balance and generosity.

options.text: Take back their allowance so they never touch it
options.rationale: ❌ Children learn stewardship by practicing with small amounts.

options.text: Forbid them from ever enjoying a small treat
options.rationale: ❌ Balance — not deprivation — is the goal.

options.text: Encourage impulse spending on everything right away
options.rationale: ❌ Misses the chance to learn moderation.

questions.question: Your child asks: 'Why is Ramadan so special?' How do you explain it?
questions.context: Ramadan is a season of spiritual renewal, family warmth, and generosity.

options.text: 'It is only about buying new clothes'
options.rationale: ❌ Misses the core spiritual and moral meaning.

options.text: 'It is only about eating huge feasts all night'
options.rationale: ❌ Reduces a spiritual month to overeating.

options.text: 'It is a month for being grumpy with everyone'
options.rationale: ❌ Ramadan teaches patience and good character.

options.text: It is the month of the Quran, fasting, drawing closer to Allah, and showing extra kindness and charity
options.rationale: ✅ Captures both the spiritual heart and the generous character of Ramadan.

questions.question: How do you teach your child the value of guarding their tongue?
questions.context: Kind, truthful speech heals hearts and builds trust.

options.text: Hit them whenever they misspeak
options.rationale: ❌ Gentle correction and modeling work best.

options.text: Use harsh language at home and expect the child to speak politely
options.rationale: ❌ Children learn speech habits first from their parents.

options.text: Practice the rule: speak good, kind words or pause thoughtfully, avoiding lies and hurtful talk
options.rationale: ✅ Gives a clear, memorable standard for everyday speech.

options.text: Tell them to blurt out every mean thought they have
options.rationale: ❌ Unfiltered insults hurt others.

questions.question: Your child hears someone using foul language on the playground. What should they do?
questions.context: Choosing not to imitate harmful speech shows maturity.

options.text: Memorize and repeat the bad words to look tough
options.rationale: ❌ Imitating foul language harms character.

options.text: Shout worse insults back at them
options.rationale: ❌ Escalates conflict and copies the bad behavior.

options.text: Mock and taunt the person
options.rationale: ❌ Taunting fuels fights.

options.text: Step away calmly, do not copy the words, and tell a trusted adult if someone is being harassed
options.rationale: ✅ Protects their own speech and handles harassment safely.

questions.question: Your child wants to gift one of their favorite toys to a neighbor's child in need. How do you respond?
questions.context: Sharing something we genuinely like is a high form of generosity.

options.text: Forbid them from ever sharing with neighbors
options.rationale: ❌ Discourages neighborly kindness.

options.text: Praise their generous heart and support their kind gift
options.rationale: ✅ Encourages empathy and the joy of giving.

options.text: Tell them to demand payment from the neighbor
options.rationale: ❌ Turns a sincere gift into a sale.

options.text: Tell them 'Never give away anything nice, only give broken things'
options.rationale: ❌ True generosity gives what is good and useful.

questions.question: How do you help your child build a loving, steady connection with the Quran?
questions.context: Small, joyful daily moments with the Quran build lifelong love.

options.text: Use punishment and shouting during Quran practice
options.rationale: ❌ Harshness creates fear instead of love for the Quran.

options.text: Say the Quran is only for one month a year
options.rationale: ❌ A small daily connection keeps its light in our lives year-round.

options.text: Make a short, warm daily time for reading and reflecting together — even a few verses
options.rationale: ✅ Consistency and warmth make Quran time a beloved daily habit.

options.text: Never open the Quran at home until adulthood
options.rationale: ❌ Early, gentle familiarity builds comfort and love.

questions.question: Your child is putting off their schoolwork. How do you connect diligence with good character?
questions.context: Doing our work conscientiously is part of trustworthiness and excellence.

options.text: Lock them in a room all evening without guidance
options.rationale: ❌ Isolation without structure breeds resentment.

options.text: Do the homework for them so they get full marks
options.rationale: ❌ Dishonest and prevents the child from learning.

options.text: Tell them schoolwork does not matter at all
options.rationale: ❌ Learning and diligence are important responsibilities.

options.text: Remind them that doing our best in learning is a trust, and help them plan manageable study blocks
options.rationale: ✅ Connects purposeful values with practical support.

questions.question: Your child looks down on a classmate whose family has less money. How do you correct this attitude?
questions.context: A person's true worth lies in their character and kindness, never their wealth.

options.text: Ignore arrogant comments
options.rationale: ❌ Arrogance needs gentle, clear correction early on.

options.text: Teach them that Allah honors people by their character and piety, never by money or clothes
options.rationale: ✅ Grounds the child in humility, fairness, and respect for all people.

options.text: Agree that wealthy people are better than others
options.rationale: ❌ Feeds arrogance and prejudice.

options.text: Tell them to avoid classmates who have less money
options.rationale: ❌ Teaches snobbery instead of brotherhood and kindness.

questions.question: How do you nurture patience in your child when something disappointing happens?
questions.context: Patience grows when parents model calm resilience and comforting remembrance.

options.text: Buy them whatever they want immediately so they never feel disappointment
options.rationale: ❌ Prevents them from building resilience.

options.text: Lose our own temper while lecturing them about patience
options.rationale: ❌ Children learn patience by seeing us practice it.

options.text: Comfort them, take calming breaths together, model patience ourselves, and look for the next constructive step
options.rationale: ✅ Models emotional and spiritual resilience in a practical way.

options.text: Snap 'Stop feeling sad right now!'
options.rationale: ❌ Patience does not mean suppressing natural feelings.

questions.question: You notice your child starting a habit of telling small lies. How do you address it effectively?
questions.context: Understanding why a child lies helps address the root cause while reinforcing honesty.

options.text: Call them a 'liar' in front of the family
options.rationale: ❌ Negative labels make children feel stuck in the behavior.

options.text: Ignore it completely and hope it vanishes
options.rationale: ❌ Gentle, consistent guidance is needed.

options.text: React with harsh physical punishment every time
options.rationale: ❌ Fear drives children to become more secretive.

options.text: Notice what triggers the lies, make it safe to tell the truth, and praise honest moments
options.rationale: ✅ Addresses the root cause and builds a positive habit of honesty.

questions.question: Your child asks: 'How do we show our love for Allah?' What is a warm, clear answer?
questions.context: Love for Allah shines through gratitude, remembrance, and kindness to His creation.

options.text: By thanking Him for His blessings, remembering Him, following what pleases Him, and being kind to others
options.rationale: ✅ Connects love for Allah to gratitude, worship, and everyday kindness.

options.text: Focus only on fear and never mention Allah's mercy and kindness
options.rationale: ❌ Children thrive when introduced to Allah's love, mercy, and wisdom.

options.text: 'We only love Allah when we get every toy we ask for'
options.rationale: ❌ Faith is built on trust and gratitude, not transactions.

options.text: 'Actions and kindness do not matter at all'
options.rationale: ❌ Sincere love shows in our character and deeds.

questions.question: How do you teach your child to be a considerate neighbor?
questions.context: Caring for neighbors and avoiding disturbing them is a core moral teaching.

options.text: Tell them neighbors do not matter
options.rationale: ❌ Respecting neighbors is an essential part of good character.

options.text: Forbid ever saying hello to neighbors
options.rationale: ❌ Warm, polite greetings build community kindness.

options.text: Let them kick balls against the neighbor's door late at night
options.rationale: ❌ Disturbs neighbors and shows disregard for their comfort.

options.text: Greet neighbors warmly, respect their rest hours, and avoid making loud noise near their home
options.rationale: ✅ Practical kindness and consideration toward neighbors.

questions.question: Your child wants to help people in need wisely. How do you guide their charitable spirit?
questions.context: Combining a generous heart with wise, safe ways of giving teaches lifelong stewardship.

options.text: Encourage their compassion and involve them in giving through trusted charities, food drives, or family giving
options.rationale: ✅ Nurtures generosity safely and thoughtfully.

options.text: Forbid them from ever giving charity
options.rationale: ❌ Charity is a core virtue to nurture.

options.text: Let a young child approach strangers alone in the street with cash
options.rationale: ❌ Giving with a parent present or through trusted channels keeps the child safe.

options.text: Tell them 'Everyone asking for help is a fraud, never help anyone'
options.rationale: ❌ Cynicism hardens the heart against charity.

questions.question: How do you teach your child to value and use their time well?
questions.context: Time is a precious blessing best honored through balance.

options.text: Let the whole day disappear into aimless scrolling without structure
options.rationale: ❌ Leaves children tired and unfulfilled.

options.text: Help them build a balanced daily rhythm for prayer, learning, active play, family time, and rest
options.rationale: ✅ A balanced rhythm teaches children how to honor their time joyfully.

options.text: Schedule every minute with study and zero playtime
options.rationale: ❌ Children need play and rest for healthy growth.

options.text: Say time management only matters for adults
options.rationale: ❌ Gentle daily routines build time skills early.

questions.question: Your child had a misunderstanding with a close friend. How do you guide them toward reconciliation?
questions.context: Making peace between friends is a deeply rewarded virtue.

options.text: Tell them to cut off every friend after one misunderstanding
options.rationale: ❌ No friendship survives without forgiveness and communication.

options.text: Yell at the friend myself
options.rationale: ❌ Escalates a childhood misunderstanding.

options.text: Encourage them to spread rumors about the friend
options.rationale: ❌ Deepens hurt and division.

options.text: Encourage them to listen to their friend's perspective, apologize for their part, and make peace warmly
options.rationale: ✅ Empathy and humility restore friendships.

questions.question: Your child sees someone mistreating a stray cat. What should they do?
questions.context: Mercy toward animals is a central teaching of Islam.

options.text: Speak up kindly if safe or call a trusted adult right away to protect the animal
options.rationale: ✅ Shows mercy to animals while keeping the child safe.

options.text: Get into a physical fight
options.rationale: ❌ Calling an adult is the safe way for a child to stop cruelty.

options.text: Say animals have no feelings so it does not matter
options.rationale: ❌ Caring for animals is a moral duty.

options.text: Laugh and watch the animal suffer
options.rationale: ❌ Cruelty to animals hardens the heart.

questions.question: How do you nurture kindness and respect toward parents (Birr al-Walidayn) in your child?
questions.context: Children learn to honor parents through mutual warmth, gratitude, and praying for one another.

options.text: Never thank our child when they help us
options.rationale: ❌ Expressing appreciation reinforces helpfulness.

options.text: Tell them kindness to family does not matter
options.rationale: ❌ Honoring parents is a foundational virtue.

options.text: Treat them with warmth, appreciate their helpfulness, and teach them to pray for their parents' well-being
options.rationale: ✅ Warmth, gratitude, and prayer nurture genuine love and respect.

options.text: Use constant guilt and harshness whenever we speak
options.rationale: ❌ Love and respect grow best in a warm home.

questions.question: Your child wants to express their creativity in school activities. How do you guide them constructively?
questions.context: Channeling talents into uplifting, respectful activities helps children shine with confidence.

options.text: Tell them values never matter in entertainment
options.rationale: ❌ Mindful choices help children stay grounded.

options.text: Focus only on what neighbors might gossip about
options.rationale: ❌ Sound values, not fear of gossip, should guide family choices.

options.text: Ban all creativity, art, and storytelling completely
options.rationale: ❌ Positive creativity is a wonderful avenue for growth.

options.text: Encourage creative talents and activities that are positive, respectful, and uplifting
options.rationale: ✅ Supports their gifts while staying true to wholesome values.

questions.question: How do you explain the importance of sincere intention (Niyyah) to your child?
questions.context: Good intentions turn everyday helpful actions into meaningful deeds.

options.text: Say 'Only do good deeds when someone is taking a photo of you'
options.rationale: ❌ Encourages showing off instead of sincerity.

options.text: Explain that Allah looks at the sincerity in our hearts — doing good to please Him and help others
options.rationale: ✅ Teaches inner sincerity rather than showing off.

options.text: Say 'Intentions do not matter at all'
options.rationale: ❌ Sincere intention is the heart of every good deed.

options.text: Only praise results and never value sincere effort
options.rationale: ❌ Valuing sincere effort builds resilience and integrity.

questions.question: Your child wants to spend all their savings on an impulse item they will forget tomorrow. How do you guide them?
questions.context: Pausing before buying teaches wisdom and avoids wastefulness.

options.text: Buy two of the impulse items right away
options.rationale: ❌ Reinforces impulsive habits.

options.text: Encourage wasting money on things that go straight to the trash
options.rationale: ❌ Wastefulness goes against wise stewardship.

options.text: Confiscate their savings without discussion
options.rationale: ❌ Guided conversation teaches financial wisdom.

options.text: Discuss together whether it is a real need or a passing whim, and try waiting a couple of days before deciding
options.rationale: ✅ A short cooling-off pause builds wise decision-making.

questions.question: Your older child finds it hard to wake up for morning prayer (Fajr). What practical steps help most?
questions.context: Practical sleep habits and warm family teamwork make waking up much easier.

options.text: Sleep early at night, set an alarm, and wake one another gently with encouragement
options.rationale: ✅ Early sleep and gentle teamwork build a sustainable morning habit.

options.text: Give up on morning routines entirely
options.rationale: ❌ Steady, gentle habits build consistency over time.

options.text: Let them stay up until midnight and then yell at them at dawn
options.rationale: ❌ Lack of sleep sets them up to struggle.

options.text: Use harsh punishment first thing in the morning
options.rationale: ❌ Gentle encouragement makes morning worship beloved.

questions.question: How do you teach your child the etiquette of knocking and asking permission before entering a closed room?
questions.context: Asking permission before entering respects privacy at home and everywhere.

options.text: Scream at them without ever modeling how to knock
options.rationale: ❌ Modeling and clear practice work best.

options.text: Practice knocking and waiting for permission — and model knocking on their door too
options.rationale: ✅ Mutual practice and role modeling make respectful privacy a natural habit.

options.text: Say manners only apply outside the house, not at home
options.rationale: ❌ Good manners begin with our own family at home.

options.text: Let everyone barge into closed rooms without knocking
options.rationale: ❌ Disregards family privacy.

questions.question: Your child asks why classmates from other backgrounds celebrate different holidays. How do you answer?
questions.context: Clear, warm pride in our own traditions goes hand in hand with kindness toward others.

options.text: Never celebrate or make our own Eids joyful at home
options.rationale: ❌ Making Eid warm and joyful strengthens a child's love for their heritage.

options.text: Snap 'Stop asking questions!'
options.rationale: ❌ Honest questions deserve calm, clear answers.

options.text: Teach hostility toward neighbors
options.rationale: ❌ Good character calls for kindness and fairness toward all neighbors.

options.text: Explain kindly that different faiths have their own holidays, while we joyfully celebrate our Islamic Eids and treat everyone with respect
options.rationale: ✅ Nurtures confident identity alongside kindness and respect.

questions.question: How do you teach your child the importance of academic honesty during school tests?
questions.context: Integrity in learning means valuing honest effort over shortcuts.

options.text: Punish them for any grade under 100% so they fear honest mistakes
options.rationale: ❌ Extreme grade pressure can push children toward dishonesty.

options.text: Teach that honest effort is what truly counts and that cheating breaks trust, while praising their real hard work
options.rationale: ✅ Connects academic honesty to integrity and values effort over perfection.

options.text: Say 'Cheating is fine as long as the teacher does not catch you'
options.rationale: ❌ Undermines integrity and self-respect.

options.text: Refuse to help them study before the test
options.rationale: ❌ Good preparation reduces the temptation to take shortcuts.

questions.question: How do you nurture a balanced, confident moral character in your child?
questions.context: Balanced upbringing weaves together faith, good character, learning, and emotional warmth.

options.text: Nurturing worship, ethics, curiosity, and emotional security together through love and role modeling
options.rationale: ✅ Holistic upbringing grows confident, compassionate young people.

options.text: Relying on harsh rules without warmth or dialogue
options.rationale: ❌ Harshness without love pushes hearts away.

options.text: Offering no moral guidance at all
options.rationale: ❌ Children need loving signposts as they grow.

options.text: Focusing on rituals while ignoring kindness and honesty
options.rationale: ❌ Worship and good character belong together.

questions.question: Your child asks: 'What does Taqwa (mindfulness of Allah) mean?' How do you explain it simply?
questions.context: Mindfulness of Allah inspires doing good in private and in public.

options.text: 'It means never smiling or enjoying life'
options.rationale: ❌ Joy, gratitude, and kindness are part of a faithful life.

options.text: Being mindful of Allah whether we are alone or with people — choosing what is good and avoiding what harms
options.rationale: ✅ A clear, inspiring explanation of inner integrity.

options.text: 'It only means wearing a specific color of clothes'
options.rationale: ❌ Taqwa lives in the heart and shows in our deeds.

options.text: 'It means never leaving the house'
options.rationale: ❌ Mindfulness of Allah guides us wherever we are in daily life.

questions.question: Your child set aside coins in a charity box, then felt tempted to spend them on candy instead. How do you guide them?
questions.context: Keeping our promises of generosity strengthens willpower and sincerity.

options.text: Remind them warmly of the joy their gift will bring to someone in need and deliver the charity together
options.rationale: ✅ Reinforces following through on good intentions.

options.text: Tell them charity never matters
options.rationale: ❌ Misses a moment to nurture generosity.

options.text: Scream at them for feeling tempted
options.rationale: ❌ Calm encouragement works much better than anger.

options.text: Throw away the charity box
options.rationale: ❌ Delivering the charity together turns intention into joyful action.

questions.question: How do you teach your child healthy reliance on Allah (Tawakkul)?
questions.context: True Tawakkul combines doing our very best effort with trusting Allah.

options.text: Tell them not to study or try at all and expect results magically
options.rationale: ❌ True reliance includes taking practical steps.

options.text: Tell them everything depends 100% on worry and stress
options.rationale: ❌ Prayer and trust bring peace after we do our best.

options.text: Encourage them to do their best preparation and effort, and then pray and trust Allah with the outcome
options.rationale: ✅ Balances practical effort with peaceful trust in Allah.

options.text: Make them terrified of ever trying anything new
options.rationale: ❌ Trust in Allah gives courage, not fear.

questions.question: What is the most important takeaway from the Tree of Character?
questions.context: Sincerity, honesty, and kindness are the roots and fruits of good character.

options.text: Kindness, honesty, and mindfulness of Allah are the heart of everyday good character
options.rationale: ✅ Captures the core values that grow a beautiful character.

options.text: Good manners do not matter as long as nobody catches you
options.rationale: ❌ True character is who we are both in public and in private.

options.text: Assume everyone around us is bad
options.rationale: ❌ Good character looks for ways to do good and treat people fairly.

options.text: Character cannot be learned or practiced
options.rationale: ❌ Good character grows stronger with every thoughtful choice we make.
